topics.title: Harnessing Chicken Power
topics.text:
KFC (Kentucky Fried Carrots) is using some shifty methods to generate electricity for its 10 stores. They are harnessing chicken power. Unsurprisingly, such Chicken power is unreliable at best (Chickens have a tendency to break out of the generator). After some analysis, KFC experts have deduced the following patterns: During the night hours, 9PM - 6AM, at any given moment, there's guaranteed to be at least 2 stores without power. The chance for the 3rd store to be without power is $\frac{8}{10}$, the chance for the 4th store to be without power is $\frac{7}{10}$, and so on until the 10th store has a $\frac{1}{10}$ chance to be without power. During the day hours, any time that is not a night hour, there is guaranteed to be at least 1 store without power. The 2nd store will have a $\frac{9}{10}$ chance to be out of power, then the 3rd store will have a $\frac{8}{10}$ chance to be without power, all the way until the 10th store has a $\frac{1}{10}$ chance to be without power. The manager of the franchise has a $\frac{1}{10}$ chance to check in during the day time, and a $\frac{1}{20}$ chance to check in during the night time. If at any time he checks in and all stores are without power, he shuts down the franchise and creates a new one called KFC (Kentucky Fried Cornbeans). How many days will the franchise be expected to last?

topics.title: What is the value of infinitely nested 0's?
topics.text:
Hello, I have a question: What is the value of $\sqrt{0+\sqrt{0+\sqrt{0+\ldots}}}$?



Let $x=\sqrt{0+\sqrt{0+\sqrt{0+\ldots}}}$. Then $x=\sqrt{0+x}$, $x^2=x$, $x^2-x=0$. The roots for that quadratic is 1 and 0. So is $\sqrt{0+\sqrt{0+\sqrt{0+\ldots}}}$ 0 or 1?



One might argue because $\sqrt{6+\sqrt{6+\sqrt{6+\ldots}}}=3$ and $\sqrt{2+\sqrt{2+\sqrt{2+\ldots}}}=2$, so $\sqrt{0+\sqrt{0+\sqrt{0+\ldots}}}=1$. However one also might argue that 0 doesn't have a value initially so the answer is 0.



What do you guys think?

I had a different solution:SolutionUsing the work formula, Tobey mows 6/5 of the lawn in a hour. I used this to make another work equation, $1=\frac{1}{2}(\frac{6}{5}+x)$ I didn't multiply by 2 since adding the rates renders them as one person. topics.title: Pls HALP!!! Overcounting Error: Can't Locate
topics.text:
I and my math tutor were going with a question like this from Intro to CP chapter 15. We found a better way to solve the issue than in the solutions manual but we obviously overcounted and got a probability of ~250%. The question was like this.



John had 3 T-shirts, 4 Jackets, and 5 Shirtsthatweresolonghecouldn'twearthem. He pulls out 5 shirts. What is the probability that he gets at least one of every kind of shirt?



Our reasoning was as follows.



Assume John gets one of each shirt. There are three possibilities for the T-shirts, and so on. $3*4*5 = 60$. Now we pick two shirts among the remaining shirts. There are 9C2(36) possibilities for the other two shirts. 36*60 = 2160. Now we find the amount of possibilities, which is 12C5 or 792. 2160/792 is not a good probability. What did we overcount?(or undercount?)
